gaps.criterion: Every mutating endpoint records a PDP decision reference
gaps.gap: THE DECISION POINT EXISTS; THE SWEEP DOES NOT. Every verdict carries a decisionRef and every evaluation a batch_ref, and the endpoint returns both, but not one of the existing mutating routes calls the PDP or records a reference yet. Concretely untouched: POST /api/leads, POST /api/leads/:id/route, /assign and /first-response, POST /api/routing-rules with its PATCH and DELETE, POST /api/sla/evaluate, and POST /api/public/leads. Nine or so handlers, each needing the same three steps - evaluate before the write, refuse on deny, persist the reference alongside the change. This was deliberately not attempted in the same task as the bundle: the two are separable, and a half-applied sweep is worse than none because some endpoints would appear governed while others silently are not, and nobody could tell which from the outside. Closing it needs a middleware or handler wrapper applied to every mutating route, a column or audit field holding the reference, and one test per route asserting the write is refused when the PDP denies.

gaps.criterion: Obligations returned by the PDP are surfaced to the caller
gaps.gap: Obligations are modelled, attached and returned: the response carries an obligations array per decision, and tests assert the two that a role grant cannot express - own_record_only on lead.work_assigned, which is the whole meaning of SOP §28's 'works ASSIGNED leads' and without which a Rep holding the grant could work every lead in the tenant, and second_party_approval on every approval-gated action. What is NOT built is anything that ENFORCES them. isUnconditionalPermit exists to make the distinction checkable, but no caller consults it, so today a permit carrying an unmet obligation is indistinguishable from a clean permit at the point of the write. That enforcement belongs with the AC2 sweep and should land in the same change, since an obligation nothing checks is documentation.
